The original sentence is grammatically correct and very clear, but depending on the tone you want to set (more formal, more concise, or more collaborative), you might want to adjust it slightly.

Here are a few options:

**Option 1: Professional & Direct (Best for email/Slack announcements)**
> "As suggested, moving forward, please include the `sql_id` in all query tuning requests to the L2/L4 teams. This will prevent unnecessary back-and-forth and speed up the investigation process."

**Option 2: Concise & Action-Oriented (Best for team meetings or documentation)**
> "To avoid delays, please ensure every query tuning request to the L2/L4 teams includes the `sql_id`."

**Option 3: Collaborative (Softer tone)**
> "As discussed, let’s make it a habit to include the `sql_id` when requesting query tuning from the L2/L4 teams. This should help minimize back-and-forth questions and get our investigations moving faster."

**Option 4: Polished Version of Your Original**
> "As suggested, going forward, please ensure we include the `sql_id` in all query tuning requests to the L2/L4 teams to avoid delays caused by additional back-and-forth communication."

**Key improvements made:**
*   **"Moving forward"** sounds slightly more professional than "going forward."
*   **"Prevent unnecessary back-and-forth"** clarifies *why* you are doing this.
*   **"Speed up"** or **"minimize delays"** is more positive and productive than "delaying the investigation."
